items.prompt: In v0.1.0, a hand-edited profile had an education entry missing its start date. Why was validating it at SAVE time the better fix than making formatDate defensive?
items.answer: The user sees the error while editing, not days later on a live job application
distractors: formatDate cannot change without breaking the MM/YYYY format used by matchers
A defensive formatDate would be measurably slower on large profiles
Save-time validation also checks that each start date precedes its end date
items.explanation: The v0.1.0 TypeError aborted the whole handleRequest, so nothing filled. v0.2.0's validateProfileDetailed checks every entry and its { month, year } parts - though date ORDER is still not checked.

items.prompt: In v0.1.0, a select with no matching option still got a rollback entry. What visible harm did 'Clear values filled here' then cause?
items.answer: It fired change events on an untouched select and inflated the Cleared count
distractors: It erased the user's own earlier selection, losing their data
It threw, because the rollback entry for the select had no stored previous value
Nothing visible: rollback skipped entries whose value was unchanged
items.explanation: The snapshot was pushed unconditionally before selectOption, so Clear rewrote the select and dispatched input/change on a field the extension never modified - on wizard pages that marks pristine fields dirty. v0.2.0 pushes the entry only after an option matched.

items.prompt: A profile saves {"java": 8}. The question reads "Years of JavaScript experience". What did v0.1.0 fill, and why was that especially bad?
distractors: Nothing
8, but with medium confidence for review
8, with medium confidence
items.explanation: text.includes(normalizedSkill) had no word boundary, so 'java' matched inside 'javascript' and filled 8 with HIGH confidence - the category promised to fill only when certain. v0.2.0 uses a whole-word regex and prefers the longest matching skill.

items.prompt: Two separate unnamed radio questions sit inside the SAME <fieldset> in v0.2.0. Are they kept apart?
items.answer: No: the structural key applies only outside a fieldset
distractors: Yes: every unnamed input gets a key from its nearest container
Yes: the shared fieldset legend differs per question
No, but only because the inputs have no form id
items.explanation: structuralKey = input.name || fieldset ? "" : getStructuralKey(input) - the finding is 'Mostly fixed' precisely because of this same-fieldset case.

items.prompt: The sidebar already masked email and phone in its display. Why was 'Copy debug JSON' still a privacy finding in v0.1.0?
items.answer: It copied every field's valueBefore - whatever the user had typed - unmasked
distractors: It included the full saved profile, password-like fields and all, in the export
It uploaded the JSON to a remote debugging endpoint for support
It copied masked values that could be reversed by inverting maskValue
items.explanation: The debug export was the one place data left the page uncontrolled. v0.2.0 replaces every non-empty valueBefore with "[redacted]" - labels and option text are still copied.

items.prompt: In v0.1.0, ShowLastResult arriving with no prior result rendered a 0/0/0/0 panel even though fields existed. Why?
items.answer: Neither Detect nor Autofill ran, so the result lists stayed empty
distractors: The sidebar renderer never received the detected fields from the content script
The page had no fillable fields at that moment
lastResult was reset to zeros on every navigation
items.explanation: Mappings were computed and discarded. v0.2.0 returns an explicit "Nothing to show yet" error instead.

items.prompt: In v0.1.0, /\b(location|city|address)\b/ matched "Email address", yet email fields filled correctly. Why was it still filed as a finding?
items.answer: Only the undocumented order of checks protected it
distractors: Email fields did receive the location value on some ATS pages
The location regex was slow on very long labels
Location matching ignored the city keyword entirely
items.explanation: The email check ran first and shielded the over-broad address pattern - load-bearing ordering that nothing documented or tested. v0.2.0 tightens location matching and pins the precedence with tests.

items.prompt: A free-text input asks "Describe your work authorization status". How does v0.2.0 treat it?
items.answer: As medium and review-only, as no option list means no yes/no
distractors: It types "Yes" with high confidence, exactly as for a Yes/No select
It skips the field permanently, recording it as an unrecognized free-text control
It fills the full saved authorization sentence from the profile
items.explanation: v0.1.0 returned true for any bare input/textarea; the fix downgrades such fields to review-only, pinned by a 'downgrades bare text inputs' test.

items.prompt: Why is writing data-eli-apply-mate-field-id onto page controls more than a hygiene issue?
items.answer: Page scripts and analytics can read it, revealing that the extension is installed
distractors: Duplicate generated ids make the browser refuse to submit the application form
The attributes break React's reconciliation and crash the page
They exceed the browser's attribute size limit on long forms
items.explanation: Still open in v0.2.0. The suggested fix keeps the element-to-id map in a WeakMap inside the content script (as the maintained repo later did).

items.prompt: Replacing <all_urls> content_scripts with activeTab plus on-click injection brought a side benefit beyond privacy. Which?
items.answer: Pages opened before an extension update always get current code
distractors: Content scripts can now read cross-origin iframes on the page
The service worker no longer needs to wake up for messages
Autofill now runs automatically whenever a known ATS application page finishes loading
items.explanation: The popup pings first and injects contentScript.js via chrome.scripting.executeScript only when nothing answers; the manifest keeps only activeTab, storage and scripting.

items.prompt: Once the popup injects on demand, why does the content script set window.__eliApplyMateLoaded before initializing?
items.answer: A second injection adds a duplicate listener and module state
distractors: Chrome refuses to execute the same script file twice without such a flag
The flag signals the site's own scripts that autofill is in progress
It persists the loaded state across page reloads, navigations and browser restarts
items.explanation: The improvement plan's third bullet: guard the content script against double injection with a module-level flag.

items.prompt: A pull request changes shouldFill to return true for "medium" as well as "high". What does it really change?
items.answer: It moves the safety boundary, so unclear mappings get written instead of reviewed
distractors: Only the sidebar's color coding for medium-confidence rows
Nothing for selects, since selectOption re-checks confidence before it writes
It only affects fields with no options, which are skipped anyway
items.explanation: Autofill calls fillField only when shouldFill(confidence) is true; everything else goes to unsure. Loosening it turns cautious fill into assisted guessing - tests must prove medium stays review-only.

items.front: Why can a plain element.value = x followed by an input event fail on React-controlled inputs (Greenhouse, Ashby)?
items.back: React overrides the value property and its internal value tracker sees no change, so the event is ignored. Call the prototype's value setter (Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(proto, 'value').set) and then dispatch input - which setNativeValue now does, rollback included.

items.front: The five site adapters only match hostnames and never implement normalizeField. What does the review recommend?
items.back: Make one real (Greenhouse is easiest: stable first_name/last_name ids) to prove the interface earns its keep, or collapse to getSiteName(url). An unused extension point is a cost: every reader must discover it does nothing.

items.front: Which single test file did the review call the highest-leverage one for this extension, and why?
items.back: A jsdom integration test that loads test-pages/fake-application.html and runs scanPage -> mapFields -> fillField -> rollbackFilled, asserting filled values and exact restoration. It exercises scanner, matchers and filler together and would have caught findings 2, 4 and 6.
